Calculate Cell Annotation Proportions per Neighbourhood

Source: R/nhood_annotation_props.R
nhood_annotation_props.Rd

Computes the proportion of cells assigned to each neighbourhood that carry each category of one or more annotation columns.

Usage

nhood_annotation_props(
  object,
  nhood_col = NULL,
  annotation_cols = "celltype",
  result_name = "nhood_annotation_props"
)

Arguments

object

A Milo or SingleCellExperiment object. Seurat objects must first be converted via as.SingleCellExperiment.

nhood_col

Character string. For plain SingleCellExperiment objects (i.e. not Milo), the name of the colData column containing neighbourhood assignments. Not required for Milo objects.

annotation_cols

Character vector of colData column names containing per-cell annotation categories to summarise per neighbourhood (e.g. cell type, lineage, cluster label). All specified columns must be present in colData; missing columns raise an error. Default: "celltype".

result_name

Character string. Key under which the results data.frame is stored in metadata(object). If an entry with this name already exists a warning is emitted and the entry is overwritten. Default: "nhood_annotation_props".

Value

The input object, with a data.frame stored in metadata(object)[[result_name]]. The data.frame has one row per neighbourhood and the following columns:

nhood

Neighbourhood identifier.

nhood_size

Total number of cells in the neighbourhood.

<annotation_col>_<category>_prop

Proportion of cells carrying each annotation category. One column per category per entry in annotation_cols — e.g. if annotation_cols = "celltype" and the column contains "CD4" and "CD8", the output columns will be celltype_CD4_prop and celltype_CD8_prop. Neighbourhoods where all cells have NA for a given annotation column have NA in all corresponding proportion columns.

Details

Object type handling

  • Milo objects: Neighbourhood membership is read directly from the sparse nhoods matrix via nhoods. Row names of this matrix must match colnames(object); a mismatch raises an error to prevent silent misassignment.

  • Plain SingleCellExperiment objects: A binary neighbourhood membership matrix is constructed internally from the column specified by nhood_col. Cells with NA assignments are excluded with a warning.

Proportion calculation

For each neighbourhood and each annotation column, per-cell labels are tabulated across all valid (non-NA) cells. Proportions are computed relative to the number of valid cells in the neighbourhood for that annotation column (i.e. each row sums to 1 over the proportion columns for a given annotation_col, excluding any NA cells). Cells with NA in a given annotation column are excluded from that column's proportions and their count is reported via a warning.

See also

nhood_annotation, nhood_diversity, nhood_shm, nhood_cdr3_convergence

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# --- Milo object, single annotation column --------------------------------
milo <- nhood_annotation_props(
  object          = milo_object,
  annotation_cols = "celltype"
)
results <- S4Vectors::metadata(milo)[["nhood_annotation_props"]]
# Output columns: nhood, nhood_size, celltype_CD4_prop, celltype_CD8_prop, ...

# --- Multiple annotation columns ------------------------------------------
milo <- nhood_annotation_props(
  object          = milo_object,
  annotation_cols = c("celltype", "lineage"),
  result_name     = "nhood_annotation_props"
)

# --- Plain SingleCellExperiment object ------------------------------------
sce <- nhood_annotation_props(
  object          = sce_object,
  nhood_col       = "community_id",
  annotation_cols = "celltype"
)
} # }
